# Latence Framework

> A model-agnostic, cloud-agnostic Python framework that turns messy enterprise documents into
> AI-ready data: a PII-handled, embedded, provenance-carrying RAG corpus and an evidence-linked
> knowledge graph, written as plain Parquet files you own.

The core names **Capabilities** — narrow typed interfaces like `Parser`, `EntityExtractor`,
`PIIDetector` — and never names a model. **Providers** fulfil them as installable plugins, so
swapping the OCR model, the extraction model or the embedder is a config key rather than a
refactor. Every Stage ships a deterministic CPU-first reference Provider, so the whole pipeline
runs offline on a laptop before any model is chosen.

If you read one file, read the agent briefing. It is written for coding agents and is ordered so
each section depends only on the ones above it.

## Start here

- [docs/agent-briefing.md](docs/agent-briefing.md): The structured briefing for coding agents — the mental model, every Provider available per Stage, the Pipeline YAML contract, the CLI, the output schema, retrieval wiring, and the six things that will burn you. Start here.
- [CONTEXT.md](CONTEXT.md): The canonical glossary. Use these terms exactly; it also lists the synonyms this project bans.
- [README.md](README.md): The project front door — what it does, the 60-second quickstart, and what is and is not measured.

## Using the framework

- [docs/quickstart.md](docs/quickstart.md): From a folder of documents to a queryable corpus, command by command.
- [docs/tutorials/index.md](docs/tutorials/index.md): Five worked tutorials — first pipeline, reading the output, retrieval, bringing your own Provider, production.
- [docs/reference/stage-contracts.md](docs/reference/stage-contracts.md): Generated Stage contracts — signatures, carriers, wiring rules, registered Providers. Regenerate with `latence contracts --write`.
- [docs/providers/catalog.md](docs/providers/catalog.md): Every registered Provider with its verified weights-and-code licence, compute and footprint.
- [docs/pipeline/index.md](docs/pipeline/index.md): What each Stage consumes and produces.

## Understanding the design

- [docs/concepts/architecture.md](docs/concepts/architecture.md): Capability, Provider, Stage, Pipeline, Runner, Storage — and where each seam sits.
- [docs/adr/index.md](docs/adr/index.md): The decision log. Every architectural decision with its rejected alternatives; read this before proposing a change to a seam.
- [docs/anatomy/index.md](docs/anatomy/index.md): The pipeline in DAG order, mechanism by mechanism.

## Extending it

- [docs/providers/README.md](docs/providers/README.md): Authoring a Provider — the five-step procedure. No core edit is required or accepted.
- [docs/tutorials/04-bringing-your-own-provider.md](docs/tutorials/04-bringing-your-own-provider.md): The hands-on version, including breaking it three ways to watch conformance catch you.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): Read this instead if you are changing *this repository* rather than using the framework — the gates, the contracts you must not break, and how to avoid a false green.

## Optional

- [docs/BENCHMARKS.md](docs/BENCHMARKS.md): Measured quality results, with the method and hardware on every row.
- [PERF-RESULTS.md](PERF-RESULTS.md): Measured throughput envelopes, plus an explicit list of what is *not* yet measured.
- [docs/guides/index.md](docs/guides/index.md): Task-focused operator guides — deployment, observability, secrets, incremental ingest, serving with Qdrant.
- [docs/CONTINUITY.md](docs/CONTINUITY.md): Bus factor, fork posture, support lifetime. Start here if you are evaluating this for adoption.
